prompt: All sounds are made by objects that are doing what?
hints: Touch your throat while you hum. What do you feel?
solution: All sounds are made by **vibrating** objects: things moving quickly back and forth, like a guitar string or your vocal cords.

prompt: What is the unit of frequency? (Give the name or the symbol.)
hints: It's named after the scientist Heinrich Hertz.
solution: Frequency is measured in **hertz (Hz)**: the number of vibrations (waves) per second.

prompt: Light travels in [[a]] lines. When light reflects off a mirror, the angle of incidence equals the angle of [[b]].
hints: Shadows have sharp edges because of the way light travels.
solution: Light travels in **straight** lines. The law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of **reflection**.

prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

right.text: How high or low a sound is
The number of vibrations per second
The material a wave travels through

hints: Amplitude is linked to loudness; frequency is linked to pitch.
solution: Pitch → how high or low; amplitude → size of the vibration; frequency → vibrations per second; medium → what the wave travels through.

prompt: Why can't sound travel through outer space?

options.text: Space is a vacuum, so there are no particles to pass on the vibrations
Space is too cold for sound
Sound travels too slowly to cross space
The Sun's light blocks the sound

feedback.b: Temperature isn't the reason. Sound needs particles.
feedback.c: Speed isn't the problem. Sound can't travel there at all.

hints: What does sound need in order to travel?
solution: Sound is passed on by particles vibrating. Space is a **vacuum**, with no particles, so sound can't travel through it. Light can, because it doesn't need a medium.

prompt: The traces show three sounds on the same settings. Which sound has the **highest pitch**?

figure.alt: Three sound wave traces on the same scales. A: two waves across the screen, small height. B: four waves across the screen, the same small height. C: two waves across the screen, about twice as tall as A.

options.text: A
B
C
They all have the same pitch

feedback.a: A has only two waves across the screen, so it has a low frequency.
feedback.c: C has the tallest waves, which makes it the loudest, not the highest pitch.
feedback.d: B has twice as many waves across the screen as A and C.

hints: Pitch depends on frequency. Which trace has the most waves across the screen?
solution: **B** has the most waves in the same time, so it has the highest **frequency**, and that means the highest pitch.

prompt: Look at the same three traces. Which sound is the **loudest**?

figure.alt: Three sound wave traces on the same scales. A: two waves across the screen, small height. B: four waves across the screen, the same small height. C: two waves across the screen, about twice as tall as A.

options.text: A
B
C
They are all equally loud

feedback.a: A's waves are short (small amplitude), so it's quiet.
feedback.b: B has the highest pitch, but its waves are no taller than A's.
feedback.d: C's waves are clearly taller than the others.

hints: Loudness depends on amplitude, the height of the wave.
solution: **C** has the tallest waves (biggest **amplitude**), so it is the loudest. It has the same pitch as A.

prompt: White light is split by a prism into a spectrum. Put the colours in order, starting with red.
hints: Remember the name "ROY G BIV".
solution: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet (**ROY G BIV**), the same order as in a rainbow.

prompt: A ray of light hits a mirror with an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
hints: Use the law of reflection.
solution: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = **35°** (both measured from the normal).

prompt: Why does a red apple look red in white light?

options.text: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colours
It absorbs red light and reflects the other colours
It gives out its own red light
It turns white light into red light

feedback.b: We see the colour that is reflected into our eyes, not the colour that is absorbed.
feedback.c: An apple isn't luminous. It doesn't make its own light.
feedback.d: The apple doesn't change light into a new colour. It reflects one colour and absorbs the rest.

hints: White light contains all the colours. Which one reaches your eye from the apple?
solution: White light contains all colours. The apple **reflects red** light into your eyes and **absorbs** the other colours, so it looks red.

prompt: A straw in a glass of water looks bent at the water's surface. What causes this?

options.text: Refraction: light changes speed and direction as it passes from water into air
Reflection: light bounces off the water's surface
The water really bends the straw
Light travels in curved lines through water

feedback.b: Reflection happens too, but the bent look comes from light changing direction as it leaves the water.
feedback.c: Take the straw out and it's still straight.
feedback.d: Light travels in straight lines inside the water. It changes direction only at the boundary.

hints: Light travels at a different speed in water than in air.
solution: Light from the straw under the water **refracts** (changes speed and direction) as it passes from water into air. Your brain assumes the light travelled in a straight line, so the underwater part looks out of place.

prompt: Select **all** the things that sound can travel through.

options.text: Air
Water
Steel
Wood
A vacuum
Outer space

hints: Sound needs particles to pass on the vibrations.
solution: Sound travels through **solids, liquids and gases** (air, water, steel, wood). It can't travel through a vacuum, and outer space is almost a perfect vacuum.

prompt: During a storm, Hemi sees a flash of lightning and hears the thunder 3 s later. Sound travels at 340 m/s in air. How far away is the lightning? (Assume the light arrives instantly.)
hints: The sound took 3 s to reach Hemi.
Distance = speed × time.
solution: $d = v \times t = 340 \times 3 = 1020$ m, about 1 km away.

prompt: Put these in order of the speed of sound through them, from **slowest** to **fastest**.
hints: Sound travels faster when the particles are closer together.
solution: Air (about 340 m/s) → water (about 1,500 m/s) → steel (about 5,000 m/s or more). The particles are closest together in solids.

prompt: When white light passes through a glass prism, it spreads out into a spectrum of colours. Why?

options.text: Each colour refracts by a different amount, so the colours separate
The prism adds colours to the white light
The glass reflects each colour off a different face
The prism absorbs the white and lets the colours through

feedback.b: The colours were already in the white light. The prism only separates them.
feedback.c: The light passes through the prism. It's refraction, not reflection, that spreads it out.
feedback.d: White light is made of the colours. There's no separate "white" to absorb.

hints: White light is a mixture of colours. Do they all bend by the same amount?
solution: White light is a mixture of colours. Each colour **refracts** (bends) by a slightly different amount in glass (violet the most, red the least), so they spread out into a **spectrum**.

prompt: On stage, a performer in a red T-shirt is lit only by a **blue** spotlight. What colour does the T-shirt look?

options.text: Black
Red
Blue
Purple

feedback.b: To look red it must reflect red light, and there is no red light here.
feedback.c: A red T-shirt absorbs blue light rather than reflecting it.
feedback.d: Colours of light don't mix on the T-shirt like paint. It can only reflect red, and there is none.

hints: A red object reflects red light only. Which colours are in the spotlight?
solution: The red T-shirt can only reflect **red** light, but the spotlight gives only **blue** light, which the T-shirt absorbs. No light is reflected, so it looks **black**.

prompt: Tama shouts towards a cliff and hears the echo 2 s later. Sound travels at 340 m/s. How far away is the cliff?
hints: An echo is sound that has travelled to the cliff **and back**.
Find the total distance travelled, then halve it.
solution: Total distance the sound travelled: $340 \times 2 = 680$ m. That's there and back, so the cliff is $680 \div 2 = 340$ m away.

prompt: Explain how the sound from a guitar string reaches your ear and lets you hear it.
modelAnswer: When the string is plucked, it vibrates back and forth. The vibrating string pushes on the air particles next to it, making them vibrate too. Each particle passes the vibration on to the next, so the sound travels through the air (the medium) as a wave, while the particles themselves only move back and forth. When the vibrations reach your ear, they make your eardrum vibrate, and you hear the sound.

rubric.criterion: The string vibrates (moves quickly back and forth)
The vibrations are passed through the air (medium) from particle to particle as a sound wave
The vibrations make the eardrum vibrate

hints: Start with the string. What is it doing?
How does the vibration get across the room?
solution: String vibrates → air particles vibrate and pass it on (sound wave through the air) → eardrum vibrates → you hear it.

prompt: A river looks shallower than it really is, which can be dangerous for swimmers. Use ideas about refraction to explain why.
modelAnswer: Light from a stone on the riverbed travels up through the water and into the air towards your eye. At the water's surface the light speeds up and bends (refracts) away from the normal. Your brain assumes light travels in straight lines, so it traces the ray straight back to a point that is higher than the real stone. The bottom appears higher, so the river looks shallower than it is.

rubric.criterion: Light from the bottom travels from water into air
It changes speed and bends (refracts) at the surface
The brain assumes light travels in straight lines, so the bottom appears higher (shallower) than it really is

hints: Which way is the light travelling: into the water or out of it?
What does your brain assume about how light travels?
solution: Light from the bottom **refracts** as it leaves the water. Your brain follows the bent ray **straight back**, so the bottom seems higher. The river looks shallower than it really is.

prompt: A ray of light passes at an angle from air into a glass block. What happens to it at the surface of the glass?

options.text: It slows down and bends towards the normal
It speeds up and bends away from the normal
It slows down and bends away from the normal
It carries on in a straight line at the same speed

feedback.b: That's what happens when light comes **out** of glass into air.
feedback.c: When light slows down, it bends towards the normal, not away.
feedback.d: Light changes speed in glass. Arriving at an angle, it also changes direction.

hints: Light travels more slowly in glass than in air.
Slowing down bends the ray towards the normal.
solution: Light travels more slowly in glass, so as it enters at an angle it **slows down and bends towards the normal**. When it leaves the glass it speeds up and bends away from the normal.

prompt: Red light is shone through a **green** filter. What comes out the other side?

options.text: Almost no light, because the green filter absorbs red light
Green light
Red light
Yellow light, because red and green mix

feedback.b: A filter can't turn red light into green. It can only let through colours that are already there.
feedback.c: A green filter absorbs red light instead of letting it through.
feedback.d: The filter doesn't add green light, so there is nothing to mix.

hints: A filter only lets through (transmits) its own colour.
Is there any green light in the red beam?
solution: A green filter transmits **only green** light and absorbs other colours. The red light is absorbed, and there's no green light in it to pass through, so **almost no light** comes out.

prompt: A research ship maps the sea floor off the New Zealand coast by sending a pulse of sound straight down. The echo returns 0.4 s later. Sound travels at 1,500 m/s in sea water. How deep is the sea there?
hints: The sound goes down to the sea floor **and back up**.
Find the total distance, then halve it.
solution: Total distance: $1500 \times 0.4 = 600$ m (down and back). Depth $= 600 \div 2 = 300$ m.
